newsitem.title: CHINA: China securities turnover sharply up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China securities turnover sharply up in 1996.

text.p: Stock trading on China's two exchanges was five times greater in 1996 than in 1995, with total turnover topping 2,100 billion yuan compared to 400 billion in 1995, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
Stock trading turnover on the Shanghai exchange rose to 911.5 billion yuan from 310.3 billion yuan while turnover on the Shenzhen exchange soared to 1,221.7 billion yuan from 93.2 billion yuan.
A total of 105 new companies made their debuts in Shanghai, bringing the total number of listed firms to 293 by the end of 1996.
In Shenzhen, 102 new companies were listed with the total standing at 237 by the end of 1996.
By the end of 1996, Shanghai's stock market capitalisation was 547.8 billion yuan, up from 252.5 billion yuan at the end of 1995.
Shenzhen's capitalisation was 436.5 billion yuan, up more than four times from 105.1 billion yuan at end-1995.

Treasury bill spot turnover in Shanghai increased more than six times to 496.2 billion yuan from 76.4 billion yuan. In Shenzhen, T-bill spot trading turnover rose to 6.7 billion yuan from 1.1 billion yuan.

T-bill repurchase turnover in Shanghai surged more than 10 times to 1,243.9 billion yuan from 117.2 billion yuan, while in Shenzhen, 1996 turnover was 56.9 billion yuan compared to 7.7 billion yuan in 1995.
Trading in listed investment funds in Shanghai was 49.7 billion yuan, up 62 percent from 30.6 billion. In Shenzhen, it increased to 106.9 billion yuan from 20.45 billion yuan.
By the end of 1996, the Shanghai stock exchange had more than 12 million registered investors and Shenzhen more than 10 million, the Shanghai Securities News said.
